about: Plan lines of the W4, W4b2, W5, W5b and W5d relay outlines (the outline:beats answers, in order): one entry per scene node, with its 1-based chapter number. A node's plan line is beat_scene_description(entry), 'title: summary'. Copied once (tpm-plan-wave5 §1(i)); tests never read the archives.

w4.title: Retained
w4.summary: Milo, freshly dead, is told by Prava that his forty-one years of optimization are an asset. For the first time in decades he feels seen, and he accepts the Reconciliations post before anyone offers him a choice, trading his bewilderment for eagerness.

w4.title: Across the Partition
w4.summary: At his new desk Milo meets Zara, who answers his throughput questions with flat instructions and a joke that is not a joke. He mistakes her courtesy for friendship, and she quietly marks him as someone worth training.

w4.title: The Bell Account
w4.summary: Milo zeroes Halvard Bell's tenure, initials the form and watches Facilities clear the desk by lunch. His question about where Bell goes gets 'He goes under' from Zara and a shrug about the appendices from Old Fen. He decides not to ask again, and his competence starts to look like complicity.

w4.title: The Locked Drawer
w4.summary: That night Milo locks the ledger in his desk drawer without knowing why. It is the first unoptimized act of his death and the first sign of an instinct he cannot yet name.

w4.title: The Memo
w4.summary: A heavy memo signed by Edric Thane summons Milo, who reads it as a promotion signal. Zara's three flat rules (bring nothing, sign nothing, stand) puncture his delight and make him afraid for the first time.

w4.title: The Chair
w4.summary: In the cold corner office Milo refuses the Lich's chair, surprising himself. Edric names his speed on the Bell account as appetite and tells him he was retained for not asking questions, not for the reason he will be kept. Milo leaves knowing he is being watched and measured by someone who was once him.

w4.title: The Column No One Explained
w4.summary: Milo takes the ledger out of his drawer and sees that Bell's tenure was not zeroed but moved, in a column no one ever explained. He turns to Zara with a question instead of an answer. She tells him he has now read an appendix and to sit down, and he crosses from employee to recruit.

w4.title: Cross-Referencing
w4.summary: Zara hands Milo the closed accounts of the past year without comment. Working back from Halvard Bell, he finds the same unexplained column on every one, and the discrepancy turns from a clerical error into a pattern.

w4.title: The Stacks
w4.summary: Looking for the receiving account, Milo goes to Records. Old Fen, half-filed himself, cheerfully finds the routing slips for him without asking why he wants them. Milo envies how little the knowledge costs Fen, and the trail now points upward.

w4.title: The Pooled Account
w4.summary: Every transfer ends in a single pooled account at the top of the org chart, coded to the CEL. Milo understands that the souls sent under are not destroyed but harvested to keep Edric Thane continuing, and that the monstrous side effect is the business.

w4.title: Draft Memo
w4.summary: Milo's first instinct is to optimize. He drafts a crisp report flagging the discrepancy to Management and imagines the recognition it will earn. Zara reads it over the partition, says nothing, and lets him keep it, so the temptation to climb is now real.

w4.title: Eleven Thousand Names
w4.summary: Milo finds Prava off the clock with a private ledger she is not permitted to keep, holding the name of every soul she has onboarded, his among them. The numbers in his report become people, Bell first among them.

w4.title: Retention
w4.summary: Milo sits in on the Retention team as they cheerfully talk a wavering soul back onto the schedule, and he recognizes his own upbeat jargon in their despair. Old Fen's contentment, which he envied, now frightens him the way it frightens Zara.

w4.title: Confetti
w4.summary: At the all-hands the quarter's single graduation is celebrated with confetti that dissolves before it lands, and Prava weeps silently. Milo realizes that the Lich chose to stay rather than take the onward, and that the system's owner does not believe its own product. His report now reads to him like Edric Thane's career.

w4.title: The Alternative
w4.summary: Back at his desk Milo cannot stand himself, and he tears up the draft. Zara finally lays out what she has built toward for two centuries: not a rebellion but a work stoppage, a union of the dead, filed procedurally. Milo accepts, and moves from would-be climber to co-conspirator.

w4.title: Signature Sheet
w4.summary: Zara moves desk to desk with a signature sheet. Prava signs first and offers her forbidden ledger as the list of names, and the isolated dead begin, quietly and on the record, to become a workforce.

w4.title: Every Soul Sent Under
w4.summary: Milo applies his gift for optimization to the right question at last. He reconciles every account ever sent under, Halvard Bell's first, with Old Fen supplying three centuries of routing slips, and the ledger now proves the harvest line by line.

w4.title: Restructuring Edric Thane
w4.summary: Using the same forms and rules Edric spent six centuries enforcing, Zara and Milo file the restructuring of the CEL's pooled account through Reconciliations itself. The machine has now been handed a correctly filed contradiction it cannot refuse.

w4.title: Reply All
w4.summary: The stoppage goes out as an all-staff email that is, for once, completely honest, and work across the Marrow District stops. Within the hour the corner office calls Milo to a quarterly review.

w4.title: Standing
w4.summary: Milo enters the corner office again, refuses the chair again, and hands Edric a single sheet: his resignation, with the reconciliation of every soul sent under attached. The power in the room shifts from reviewer to reviewed.

w4.title: The Review
w4.summary: Edric reads it with total thoroughness, searching for an error and finding none. He recognizes his own younger self in the clerk before him and admits, in ledger language, that he stayed because he feared the onward. The Lich's certainty breaks.

w4.title: Filed Correctly
w4.summary: Under his own terms of service, Edric Thane countersigns the reconciliation, files it correctly and goes onward. The pooled account is zeroed and the harvested tenure is returned.

w4.title: Plain Language
w4.summary: Aeon is left to explain itself to its customers in plain language. Back at his desk Milo finds his boredom was a wound where his questions used to be, and he asks one. Zara, two centuries alone, answers him and has company.

w4b2.title: Mid-Sentence
w4b2.summary: Milo dies on a Tuesday halfway through complaining that a meeting could have been an email, and wakes in the intake atrium still mid-sentence; the complaint, unfinished, is the last thing of his life he owns, and he is already more interested in the queue system than in being dead.

w4b2.title: Strong Culture Fit
w4b2.summary: Prava slides a laminated org chart across a laminate desk and tells him, warmly, that he has been retained and will start Monday in Reconciliations; Milo, told for the first time that his boredom is an asset, says yes before anyone offers him a choice, and Prava remembers his name in a way he does not yet find strange.

w4b2.title: Lanyard, Desk, Mentor
w4b2.summary: Orientation hands Milo a lanyard, a vocabulary sheet and an org chart on which the CEL looks like a subsidiary; he is seated at a desk beside Zara Okafor, who does not look up, and he mistakes her flat courtesy for the beginning of a friendship.

w4b2.title: The Fastest Closer
w4b2.summary: Under Zara's terse instructions Milo learns to review, zero and file restructured accounts, and becomes the fastest closer on the floor; the newsletter names him, the gray coffee tastes like belonging, and he likes being good at it.

w4b2.title: Confetti That Dissolves
w4b2.summary: At the all-hands in the bedrock amphitheatre the quarter's single graduation is announced with confetti that dissolves before it lands; Milo applauds the proof that the system works, glimpses Prava weeping off the clock, and notices Zara not clapping.

w4b2.title: Halvard Bell
w4b2.summary: Milo opens the account of Halvard Bell, a former dentist with ninety years in Retention, restructured at nine that morning; the tenure on file does not match ninety years of labor, and the difference has gone somewhere the form has no box for.

w4b2.title: Where Did It Go
w4b2.summary: Milo turns to Zara and, for the first time in his life or death, asks the next question: where did the tenure go? Zara finally looks up, and does not answer, and the not-answering is the start of something.

w4b2.title: Try Records
w4b2.summary: Zara answers Milo's question with an instruction instead of an explanation, sending him to Records with Halvard Bell's file number; Milo understands for the first time that his trainer has been waiting for him to ask.

w4b2.title: Old Fen Files Himself
w4b2.summary: In the stacks Milo meets Old Fen, so long in Records that he has begun to file himself, who tells him without looking up that nobody reads the appendices and hands him the one that matters; Milo envies Fen's contentment, and the envy frightens him a little.

w4b2.title: Printed in Grief
w4b2.summary: Reading the appendix, including the clauses that only show under grief, Milo learns that souls sent under are not destroyed but harvested, their tenure extracted upward; he recognises Halvard Bell's form as one of his own closings and realises he has been doing the harvesting, efficiently, for months.

w4b2.title: Follow the Tenure
w4b2.summary: Milo runs the reconciliation he was hired never to run, end to end across every account he has closed, and finds every restructured soul's tenure flowing to a single pooled account at the top of the org chart, labelled only CEL; the subsidiary he pictured on his first day dissolves.

w4b2.title: The CEL Is a Person
w4b2.summary: Zara, asked flatly, confirms that the CEL is a person, Edric Thane, a clerk who climbed, pooled tenure and bought continuance instead of the onward; Milo hears his own career in the story and feels, shamefully, a flicker of admiration.

w4b2.title: Discrepancy Report
w4b2.summary: Milo drafts a beautifully formatted report to Management flagging the discrepancy and proposing efficiencies, the kind that would make him visible and promotable, the same climb Edric Thane once made; Zara reads over the partition and says nothing, and lets him hold it.

w4b2.title: The Signature Sheet
w4b2.summary: When Milo cannot stand himself any longer, Zara lays a signature sheet on his desk, short and already half full, and asks him to choose; Milo deletes the report, and becomes, without a title, the first analyst in Reconciliations to stop being useful on schedule.

w4b2.title: Signatures
w4b2.summary: Zara works the building one desk at a time, Retention's cheerful despairers, Old Fen's Records, the coffee-station regulars, and the signature sheet grows from a page into a binder; Milo learns that organising is mostly listening, and that the dead have been waiting a long time to be asked.

w4b2.title: Reconciling Everyone
w4b2.summary: Milo begins the reconciliation of every soul ever sent under, starting with Halvard Bell, applying the Pipeline's own rules to restore each account's tenure; the work is the most absorbing he has ever done, and for once he knows exactly what it is for.

w4b2.title: Eleven Thousand Names
w4b2.summary: The records have gaps Aeon made on purpose; Prava, who is not permitted a private ledger, brings hers, eleven thousand names she has kept by hand, and the reconciliation becomes complete; Milo understands what her warmth at his intake actually was.

w4b2.title: Reply All
w4b2.summary: The all-staff email goes out, for once completely honest about what the Pipeline does, and the Marrow District stops hoping on schedule; within the hour a summons arrives for Milo to attend the quarterly review in the corner office of Edric Thane.

w4b2.title: The Corner Office
w4b2.summary: Milo enters the one office no employee returns from unchanged and meets Edric Thane, measured and courteous, who reviews Milo's excellent closing record and offers him the climb; Milo sees exactly who he would have become.

w4b2.title: One Sheet of Paper
w4b2.summary: Milo hands over a single sheet, his resignation, with the reconciliation attached; Edric reads it line by line, searching for an error, and finds none: under his own rules the pooled account zeroes out and every harvested soul's tenure is restored.

w4b2.title: Filed Correctly
w4b2.summary: Edric Thane, a clerk undone by a clerk, admits the fear of the onward that kept him six hundred years, countersigns the filing, files it correctly, and goes; the office is empty, and the Pipeline is left holding its own word.

w4b2.title: Plain Language
w4b2.summary: Aeon must explain to its customers in plain language what it does; Milo returns to his desk, bored again and knowing now that the boredom was a wound where his questions used to be, and Zara, across the partition, looks up and stays.

w5.title: Retained
w5.summary: Milo, dead mid-sentence on a Tuesday, is slid a laminated org chart by Prava and told his skills are a strong culture fit; for the first time in decades he feels seen, and says yes before anyone offers him a choice.

w5.title: The Desk Across the Partition
w5.summary: In Reconciliations, Zara Okafor answers his eager questions about throughput and dashboards with flat instructions and tells him to read the appendices; Milo laughs at a bleak line she did not mean as a joke, and decides she is his friend.

w5.title: Throughput
w5.summary: Milo closes his first queue of restructured accounts faster than anyone in memory, zeroing tenure with a pleasure he mistakes for purpose; Old Fen's remark that nobody reads the appendices goes past him, and Zara watches without comment.

w5.title: The Bell Account
w5.summary: Milo zeroes the tenure of Halvard Bell, ninety years in Retention, in under four minutes; Facilities clears Bell's desk before lunch, and when Milo asks where Bell actually goes, Zara tells him to write 'under' and nothing else. That night he locks the ledger in his drawer without knowing why.

w5.title: The Memo
w5.summary: A memo heavy enough to have its own gravity arrives signed by Edric Thane; Milo reads it as a career win, Zara tells him it is not normal and gives him rules: bring nothing, sign nothing, stand. His excitement acquires its first crack of fear.

w5.title: The Chair
w5.summary: In the cold corner office the Chief Executive Lich offers Milo a chair, names his speed as appetite and warns that he was retained for not asking questions; Milo stays standing and asks whether there is a reason he will be kept, the first refusal and first real question of his death.

w5.title: Moved, Not Zeroed
w5.summary: Back at his desk Milo unlocks the ledger and finds in an unexplained column that Bell's tenure was not zeroed but moved; he brings the discrepancy to Zara, who tells him he has finally read an appendix and that they have a great deal of paperwork to do.

w5.title: After Hours
w5.summary: Milo stays past a shift no clock measures, pulling his own closed accounts and finding that every one, Halvard Bell's first among them, has the same moved column; the discrepancy stops being a one-off and becomes a pattern.

w5.title: Records
w5.summary: Needing older ledgers, Milo goes to Records, where Old Fen retrieves them without looking up and seems not to mind that he has begun to file himself; Milo envies his peace and is unsettled by the envy.

w5.title: The Top of the Org Chart
w5.summary: With Zara answering only the questions he has earned, Milo follows every moved column to a single pooled account belonging to the CEL and realizes the letters stand for a person, Edric Thane, kept continuing on the harvested hope of the souls sent under. The side effect is the business; the rest is overhead.

w5.title: Executive Summary
w5.summary: Milo's instinct is to optimize: he drafts a tidy report flagging the discrepancy for Management, imagining the recognition, and does not notice he is walking the path Edric Thane walked six hundred years ago. Zara reads it, says nothing, and hands it back.

w5.title: Eleven Thousand Names
w5.summary: Returning to Intake on an errand, Milo discovers Prava's forbidden private ledger of every soul she has onboarded and learns she weeps off the clock at each graduation as her only proof that leaving is possible; the names in his own closed accounts become people.

w5.title: Retention
w5.summary: Sitting in on the cheerful Retention team as they talk the wavering back onto the schedule, and then on Old Fen's contented filing, Milo sees the two endpoints the Pipeline offers, hope spent and hope forgotten, and can no longer stand the report in his drawer.

w5.title: The Signature Sheet
w5.summary: Zara finally lays out the plan she has spent two centuries building: not a rebellion the Lich could file as a threat, but a work stoppage, a union of the dead, made of paperwork. Milo tears up his report and signs, choosing the harder turn.

w5.title: Sign Here
w5.summary: Zara moves the signature sheet department by department in the gaps between quotas; Prava signs first, with the private ledger of eleven thousand names as her witness list, and the dead who have always been alone discover they are no longer the only one who knows.

w5.title: Every Soul Sent Under
w5.summary: Milo puts his forty-one years of optimizing to the one use that matters, reconciling every account the Pipeline ever sent under and drafting the restructuring of the CEL's pooled account under the Pipeline's own rules; Old Fen, asked for the oldest ledgers, hands them over and, for once, looks up.

w5.title: The Crack
w5.summary: Reading the oldest entries, Milo and Zara find that Edric Thane once had enough tenure to graduate and chose continuance instead; the Lich does not believe in the onward he sells, and a machine whose owner fears its product can be undone by saying so out loud.

w5.title: Drafts
w5.summary: Zara drafts the all-staff email announcing the work stoppage, completely honest for once, and Milo drafts his own resignation; they set the filing for the quarterly review, committing past the point where either could restructure their way back.

w5.title: Stoppage
w5.summary: The all-staff email goes out and the Marrow District stops hoping on schedule: desks sit idle, Retention stops retaining, and the Pipeline finds no form on which to file a refusal this correct.

w5.title: One Sheet of Paper
w5.summary: At his quarterly review Milo again declines the chair and hands Edric Thane his resignation, with the reconciliation of every soul sent under attached, Halvard Bell's account among them, tenure restored and the pooled account zeroed by Edric's own rules.

w5.title: Filed Correctly
w5.summary: Edric reads it, finds no error, and recognizes the clerk he once was; with the terrible mercy of a man who understands it completely, he initials the restructuring of his own account, files it correctly, and goes onward.

w5.title: Plain Language
w5.summary: The Pipeline, for the first time in three hundred years, must explain to its customers in plain language what it does; Milo gets his boredom back and understands it was a wound where his questions used to be, Old Fen looks up from his filing, and Zara, at the next desk, finally has company.

w5b.title: A Meeting That Could Have Been an Email
w5b.summary: Milo dies mid-sentence complaining about a pointless meeting and opens his eyes in a queue he instinctively starts optimizing; the shift from life to death registers to him as a change of employer rather than a loss.

w5b.title: Strong Culture Fit
w5b.summary: Prava slides a laminated org chart across the desk and tells Milo his forty-one years of pointless optimization are an asset; for the first time in decades he feels seen, and he accepts the placement in Reconciliations before anyone thinks to offer him a choice.

w5b.title: Lanyard, Desk, Mentor
w5b.summary: Milo is issued a lanyard and walked into the windowless, clockless Marrow District, where he gushes to his assigned trainer Zara Okafor; her flat, unbroken courtesy is the first thing he misreads as friendship.

w5b.title: Sometimes It's Quieter
w5b.summary: Over gray coffee, Milo asks a stream of eager questions and Zara answers only the ones that teach him to watch; she notes something about him that he does not see her note, and the recruitment quietly begins.

w5b.title: Quota
w5b.summary: Zara drills Milo on tenure, billable versus non-billable work and the newsletter's approved vocabulary; he masters the forms faster than anyone she has trained, and the speed pleases him more than it should.

w5b.title: Confetti That Dissolves
w5b.summary: At the all-hands in the bedrock amphitheater one soul graduates to applause; Milo is moved, Zara is not, and he glimpses Prava weeping at the back, which he files away without understanding it.

w5b.title: Halvard Bell's Account
w5b.summary: Milo is handed his first restructured account: Halvard Bell, a former dentist who spent ninety years in Retention and was restructured at nine that morning. He zeroes the tenure cleanly and only afterwards notices that the destination field reads 'under'.

w5b.title: Nobody Reads the Appendices
w5b.summary: Milo asks Old Fen in Records what 'under' means; Fen points him to the appendices, and what Milo reads makes clear that Halvard Bell did not go onward. Back at his desk he opens the next file and closes it perfectly, deciding to stay good at the job, while Zara, without looking up, watches him choose.

w5b.title: Top of the Curve
w5b.summary: Milo's first performance review ranks him the department's best closer on a curve built so someone must fail; he is delighted, and only later learns which colleague the curve put at the bottom, which he decides is not his to circle back on.

w5b.title: Records Requests
w5b.summary: Fetching files from Records, Milo envies Old Fen's untroubled contentment and asks how he stopped minding; Fen's answer, that he has begun to file himself, makes contentment look less like peace and more like a warning Milo does not heed.

w5b.title: Read It Again
w5b.summary: Zara slides a closed account back onto Milo's desk and says only 'Read it again'; he finds nothing wrong, then finds a date that does not match, and for the first time the forms show him something they did not ask about.

w5b.title: A Routine Account
w5b.summary: Closing an ordinary restructured file, Milo's tally comes up short: the soul's tenure leaves the ledger faster than any labour or fee schedule can explain, and his professional pride will not let the discrepancy go.

w5b.title: Follow the Tenure
w5b.summary: Pulling a quarter's worth of closed accounts, Halvard Bell's among them, Milo traces every missing fraction to the same destination: a single pooled account at the top of the org chart, and the account holder's initials are CEL.

w5b.title: Low-Hanging Fruit
w5b.summary: Milo understands that souls sent under are harvested to keep Edric Thane, the Chief Executive Lich, continuing, and his first instinct is not horror but opportunity: he drafts a crisp report to Management that could get him promoted, while Zara, across the partition, does not look up.

w5b.title: Draft Saved
w5b.summary: Milo polishes his report for Management for days while Zara says nothing; the longer she lets him sit with it, the more clearly he sees himself as the next Edric Thane, until he cannot stand to send it.

w5b.title: The Ledger She Isn't Allowed
w5b.summary: Zara takes Milo to Prava, who shows him her forbidden ledger: the name of every one of eleven thousand souls she onboarded, Halvard Bell's among them. The numbers on Milo's spreadsheet become people, and he deletes the draft.

w5b.title: Not a Rebellion
w5b.summary: Zara finally explains herself, briefly: a sword threatens the Lich, a signature sheet threatens the terms of service. She lays out two centuries of organising toward a union of the dead and a procedurally flawless work stoppage, and Milo signs first.

w5b.title: Every Appendix
w5b.summary: With Old Fen supplying the obscure clauses and Prava's names matched to Milo's numbers, they prepare the reconciliation of every soul ever sent under, closing the CEL's pooled account under the Pipeline's own rules; even Fen, content for centuries, initials it.

w5b.title: All-Staff
w5b.summary: The work stoppage begins with an all-staff email that is, for once, entirely honest; the Marrow District goes quiet in a new way, and Milo is summoned to the quarterly review in the corner office.

w5b.title: Mr. Voss
w5b.summary: In the office no employee leaves unchanged, Edric Thane receives Milo with measured, ledger-bound courtesy and recognises in him the clerk he once was; Milo, stammering through his corporate hedges, holds out a single sheet of paper anyway.

w5b.title: Filed Correctly
w5b.summary: Edric reads Milo's resignation and the attached reconciliation that restores every harvested soul's tenure and zeroes his pooled account; finding it procedurally flawless, the clerk undone by a clerk countersigns it and goes onward, to the place he spent six centuries afraid of.

w5b.title: Plain Language
w5b.summary: Back on the floor, Aeon Holdings must explain to its customers exactly what the Pipeline does; Milo gets his boredom back and recognises it as the wound where his questions used to be, and Zara, for the first time in two hundred years, has company.

w5d.title: Retained
w5d.summary: Prava slides a laminated org chart across the desk and tells Milo that his skills are a strong culture fit. Milo, who has never been told his boredom was valuable, feels seen and agrees before anyone asks. He goes from newly dead to employed.

w5d.title: Read the Appendices
w5d.summary: At the next desk in Reconciliations, Zara tells him to read the appendices and thank no one. Milo hears it as mentorship and pitches trackers and quick wins at her. She gives him one rule: close what is in his queue and open nothing else. The rule plants the first boundary he will later cross.

w5d.title: Four Minutes
w5d.summary: The Bell account arrives. Milo zeroes Halvard Bell's tenure, initials the form, and Bell is sent under by lunch while Facilities clears his desk. Milo's eager question about where Bell goes gets only 'He goes under' from Zara and a remark from Old Fen that nobody reads the appendices. Milo is unsettled for the first time, though he could not say why.

w5d.title: The Drawer
w5d.summary: That night Milo locks the ledger in his desk drawer, which nobody asked him to do. It is his first act of keeping something back from the Pipeline.

w5d.title: The Memo
w5d.summary: A heavy memo signed by Edric Thane summons Milo personally. Milo takes it as a career signal. Zara tells him it is not normal: bring nothing, sign nothing, and stand if offered a chair. Her warning is the first time she has openly taken his side.

w5d.title: Appetite
w5d.summary: In the cold corner office the Lich invites Milo to sit, and Milo, to his own surprise, stays standing. Edric names Milo's four-minute close of the Bell account as appetite rather than diligence, and warns that the reason Milo was retained is not the reason he will be kept. Milo leaves knowing he is being watched and measured.

w5d.title: Moved, Not Zeroed
w5d.summary: Milo unlocks his drawer and finds that, in a column nobody has explained to him, Bell's tenure was moved rather than zeroed. Bringing it to Zara as a discrepancy in search of a stakeholder, he hears her say he has finally read an appendix and should sit down because they have paperwork to do. Milo goes from obedient clerk to someone who knows.

w5d.title: Ink That Shows Under Grief
w5d.summary: Zara gives Milo the full contract, appendices included, and teaches him to read the clauses printed in ink that shows only under grief. Their lessons change from training in closing accounts to training in noticing.

w5d.title: Following the Column
w5d.summary: Milo requests old closed files from Records, where Old Fen hands them over without curiosity, and runs the moved-tenure column back through every restructured account. All of it flows upward into a single pooled account at the top of the org chart. A suspicion becomes a sum.

w5d.title: Everything Else Is Overhead
w5d.summary: Milo names it aloud to Zara: the souls sent under are not destroyed but harvested, their hope funneled upward to keep Edric Thane continuing. The harvest is not a side effect of the business; it is the business. Milo's picture of his job, and of himself as good at it, collapses.

w5d.title: The Draft
w5d.summary: Milo's reflex takes over and he begins a crisp memo reporting the discrepancy upward, already imagining being seen and promoted. Zara reads it over his shoulder and says nothing, letting him write it. The temptation to climb as Edric once did is now on paper.

w5d.title: Eleven Thousand Names
w5d.summary: Milo returns to the intake atrium and finds that Prava remembers every soul she has onboarded and keeps their names in a private ledger she is not permitted to have, Halvard Bell's among them. The harvested souls stop being account numbers to him.

w5d.title: Content
w5d.summary: Milo watches Old Fen filing himself into Records, envies his contentment, and then watches the cheerful Retention team talk a wavering soul back onto schedule. He sees what he becomes if he stays good at his job, and envy turns to fear.

w5d.title: Confetti That Dissolves
w5d.summary: At the all-hands graduation in the bedrock amphitheater, the quarter's single graduate leaves to applause and Prava weeps off the clock. Milo realizes that the Lich, the one soul ever able to buy the onward, chose to stay, and that the owner of the machine does not believe in its product.

w5d.title: In
w5d.summary: Back at his desk, Milo cannot stand the memo or the version of himself who wrote it. He tears it up and tells Zara he is in. She offers him her alternative: not a rebellion but a union of the dead and a procedurally impeccable work stoppage. Milo is no longer climbing; he is organized.

w5d.title: The Signature Sheet
w5d.summary: Zara takes a signature sheet from department to department. Prava signs first and offers her forbidden ledger of eleven thousand names as the membership roll. Even Old Fen, after a long pause, files his own name. The dead stop being alone, which is the one thing the curve was built to prevent.

w5d.title: Starting With Bell
w5d.summary: Milo reopens the Bell account and reconciles it correctly, restoring Halvard Bell's tenure line by line under the Pipeline's own rules, then works through every soul ever sent under. The speed the Lich called appetite now runs in reverse.

w5d.title: Restructuring the Account at the Top
w5d.summary: Milo files the restructuring of Edric Thane's pooled account through Reconciliations, the department built to close accounts. Zara checks every field twice, because the Lich can survive a threat but not a correctly filed contradiction. The undoing becomes a document waiting for review.

w5d.title: Reply All
w5d.summary: The work stoppage goes out as an all-staff email that is, for once, completely honest about what the Pipeline does, and the Marrow District stops hoping on schedule. A memo comes back summoning Milo to a quarterly review. The confrontation is now set.

w5d.title: Stand
w5d.summary: Milo enters the corner office, is offered a chair again and stands, this time on purpose. He hands Edric Thane a single sheet: his own resignation, with the procedurally flawless reconciliation of every soul ever sent under attached. The power in the room passes from the reviewer to the reviewed.

w5d.title: Files It Correctly
w5d.summary: Edric reads it the way a clerk reads, recognizes his younger self in Milo, and finds no error. Undone by a clerk under his own terms of service, he initials the reconciliation, his pooled account zeroes, and he goes onward, the thing he spent six centuries afraid of.

w5d.title: Plain Language
w5d.summary: Back in Reconciliations, Milo's boredom returns and he understands it was never a personality but a wound where his questions used to be. Zara, after two centuries of anger, has company. The Undeath Pipeline must now explain to its customers, in plain language, what it does.
